component.name: Warcraft Recorder
component.summary: Automatically record and review World of Warcraft gameplay

description.p: Warcraft Recorder captures World of Warcraft activities and keeps a local library for video review with combat-log metadata.
Native Linux and Wayland releases are distributed through the project's signed Flatpak remote. Recordings and configuration remain local.

screenshot.caption: Native library and player view with combat recording status.

description.p: Added recording support for the new Midnight patch 12.1 raid encounters and Mythic+ dungeon rotation.
Screen-capture errors now disappear once recording recovers through an automatic restart, rearming, or capture-target reselection.
Combat-log timestamps now follow the system timezone and daylight saving time instead of UTC, and a stale saved-recording event can no longer be attached to a newer recording.

The installer now checks that the session can record before it finishes: X11 sessions, a missing screen-capture portal, and a stopped PipeWire are each called out with the fix. Restarting the media worker no longer deadlocks when it is busy, and folder validation no longer overwrites existing probe files.
After an update the app now opens a "What's new" window listing the changes that went into the version it just installed.

The post-migration notice now stays dismissed instead of returning on every start, the recording and combat-log folders are highlighted until they are selected, and the advanced combat logging warning no longer fires when the sandbox simply cannot read the game's configuration file.

First release of the native Linux/Wayland application. It replaces the Electron build with lower resource use, a Wayland-native interface, and Flatpak updates. Legacy settings are imported once; the recording folder and World of Warcraft log folders have to be selected again so the sandbox can reach them.
